reading.body:
Flexential Jacksonville publishes 1.39 MW of critical load UPS capacity, ranking fourth among Florida's four data centers with disclosed power figures and representing 15 percent of the state's total published capacity.

The facility holds certifications for PCI DSS, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, and ISO 27001, which qualify it for regulated workloads in finance and healthcare. These attestations do not indicate whether the site currently hosts AI tenants, GPU infrastructure, or accelerators. The certifications establish baseline compliance but reveal nothing about actual AI training or inference workload presence.

At 1.39 MW across 35,184 square feet, this facility operates at a scale far below the megawatt-plus thresholds now standard for AI-focused compute campuses. Florida has 13 mapped data center facilities overall, but only four publish power capacity at all. The absence of published cooling specifications, electrical redundancy architecture, or infrastructure detail designed for high-density GPU density means the site's actual constraint on AI workload is unknowable from available data.
